title: Rehabilitation in Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury – A Mixed-Methods Study on Assessing the Outcome Quality of Rehabilitation Measures for Activity-Oriented, Functional Developments in Individuals with Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury in Clinical and Non-Clinical Settings
summary:
Every year, many people suffer spinal cord injuries. In Germany, this affects about 25 out of one million people. Because more and more older individuals are affected and often have multiple health conditions, treatment becomes more challenging. In addition, patients now spend less time in specialized clinics, which means therapy has to be completed in a shorter period.
What does the study examine?
The study looks at how walking ability develops in people with incomplete spinal cord injury—both during their hospital stay and later at home.
How is this done?
Researchers use two types of data: numbers (e.g., measurements) and personal experiences (e.g., interviews) to gain a complete picture.
Why is this important?
The results aim to improve treatment, develop new ideas for rehabilitation, and better plan follow-up care.

interventions.name:
People with incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI) in inpatient and outpatient settings
Retrospective and prospective mixed-methods study design.

Quantitative research approach:
Retrospective study plan: Lokomat data analysis for the years 2019-2024 based on three defined test points (T1, T2, T3).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
incomplete spinal cord injury
Inpatient stay at the Spinal Cord Injury Center, BG Hospital Hamburg
Ability to participate in Lokomat training
Ability to consent
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing conditions that could impair compliance
Motor and sensory complete spinal cord injury (AIS type A or B)
